title: All in One: Multi-Task Prompting for Graph Neural Networks

problem.claim: Graph applications involve diverse node-level, edge-level, and graph-level tasks.

gap.claim: Pre-training pretexts are often incompatible with diverse graph tasks and may cause negative transfer to specific applications.

contributions.claim: A multi-task prompting method is proposed for graph models.
Graph prompts and language prompts are unified through prompt tokens, token structure, and inserting patterns.
Meta-learning is used to learn an initialization for multi-task graph prompts, with the aim of improving reliability and generality across tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe their multi-task prompting method for graph models as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report conducting extensive experiments whose results demonstrate the superiority of their method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pre-training and fine-tuning are used to transfer general graph knowledge when application-specific graph annotations are limited.
Diverse graph task levels make pre-training pretexts incompatible with multiple tasks and can produce negative transfer.
The work studies graph prompting, inspired by prompt learning in NLP, to narrow the gap between pre-trained models and graph tasks.
The framework unifies graph and language prompts, reformulates downstream problems as graph-level tasks, and uses meta-learning for prompt initialization.
The authors report extensive experiments demonstrating method superiority.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are specified.
The abstract does not detail the prompt architecture or meta-learning algorithm.
The scope and conditions of the reported superiority are unspecified.
